about: Exceptions for scripts/offline-scan.mjs. Keep it small and narrow: every entry names the file it applies to where it can, what it lets through, and why that is not a network load and not a price or upgrade prompt. A URL in a load position (src=, srcset, srcdoc, <link href>, url(), image-set(), @import, fetch(, …) is never allowed, whatever this file says. No entry passes a URL whose path ends in a resource extension (.png, .js, .css, .woff2, …) unless it sets allowResourcePath and its match names that one exact URL (^…$, no wildcards). A library bump that brings a URL on a new host fails the scan until a reviewed entry here names it.
budgetWhy: Size budget for Resources/Zest (ADR 0015, risk 3): 8 MB. Measured at 6.81 MB on 2026-11-13 and, with the in-app switches, 6.89 MB (7,225,942 bytes, 143 files) on 2026-11-14, of which Mermaid is 3.41 MB and the fonts 2.00 MB; the headroom covers a library bump, not a new library.

urls.why: XML namespace names (xmlns): identifiers, never fetched
the DOCTYPE system identifier in ZestMail's exported email; browsers never fetch a DTD
the RFC 2606 example domain: the link targets in ZestMail's sample blocks and footer, and a link in Zest MD's sample document. Links, not loads; only these exact pages
a placeholder in the Open Graph snippet ZestImage copies for the user's own site (.example is reserved); text the user pastes, never loaded here
the website field of ZestMail's sample brand, shown as a footer link in the email; a link is not a load
linkify-it, inlined in Zest MD: prefixes a bare www. address with http:// to make a link's href; a link is not a load
"http://" + text: linkify-it, inlined in Zest MD, normalizing a bare www. address into a link's text; a link is not a load
comments in the copy of highlight.js inlined in Zest MD
"http://" + text: marked's autolinker inside Mermaid, making a link's href from a bare www. address; a link is not a load
project, issue and release links in library comments and error messages, and each font project's home page in fonts.json; pages people read, never fetched
a source-code citation in a comment inside Mermaid (a GitHub page about event.js, not the file)
Chevrotain (Mermaid's parser library) documentation links in its error messages
Langium (Mermaid's grammar library) documentation link in an error message
license banners of the libraries bundled inside Mermaid (lodash, Underscore, jQuery, stylis and others)
reference links in license banners and a Chevrotain error message inside Mermaid
the attribution field of a font's license metadata (DM Serif Display) in fonts.json; never fetched
